[untitled BTM module] These genes outline the terminal stages of erythroid differentiation, in which a committed progenitor remodels its membrane and cytoskeleton, condenses and expels its nucleus, and emerges as a deformable red cell able to survive repeated passage through capillaries and the spleen. Several members are plasma-membrane carriers that set how nutrients and ions cross epithelial barriers: GLUT2 moves glucose across hepatocyte and beta-cell membranes and underlies glucose sensing, the organic cation transporter SLC22A2 clears cationic drugs and metabolites in the proximal tubule, SLC6A13 imports betaine and GABA, and the copper-transporting ATPase ATP7B loads copper onto ceruloplasmin and excretes excess into bile, its loss causing Wnson disease.
